name: Meridian Lab 5.1 - Ali & Usama
description: IA 642 Lab 5.1 Meridian campaign mapping (ATT&CK v19).

techniques.comment: E2: nine Event ID 4769 requests for one SPN (MSSQLSvc/sqlapp01...), RC4 (0x17), ~3.5 minutes, from an ordinary logged-in account; ticket cracked offline. Matches ATT&CK Kerberoasting.

E1: 143 outbound TLS sessions to sync-update.meridian-relay.test:443 on a ~8-minute timer. ATT&CK Web Protocols covers application-layer C2 over web ports; no PCAP so HTTP content inside TLS is unconfirmed.

Rejected. ATT&CK requires asymmetric crypto used to conceal C2 rather than relying on inherent protocol protection. E1 is ordinary TLS 1.2 with a publicly trusted cert — that is inherent TLS, not extra asymmetric channel encryption.
Rejected. ATT&CK Scheduled Transfer is about scheduling data exfiltration. E1 shows timed C2 check-ins (~540-610 B send / 1.2-1.4 KB receive), not evidence that Meridian data left on a schedule.
Rejected for this campaign. E4 failed SSH on vpn-gw-01 and corp-backup-01 has no time/account/host link to E1-E3; corp-backup success matches a known nightly password-change job.

E3: stand-in shows MZ marker, MeridianLoader banner, decode-stub-shaped bytes (90 90 90 31 C0...), and embedded C2 host. Fits Obfuscated Files parent, but file is a defanged stand-in so confidence stays possible/contested.

Optional E3: filename svcupdate.bin and banner MeridianLoader/2.1 resemble a legitimate Meridian update component. Match Legitimate Name/Location is plausible but naming alone is not strong confirmation.
